verdict.headline: Tech stocks have their worst day since August on a report that OpenAI earns less than thought
verdict.label: Close Thu: S&P 500 7,765.36 (-0.47%), Nasdaq 27,193.34 (-1.25%), Dow 51,231.64 (+0.10%); chip index -3.4%; 10Y ~5.23% (-5 bp), 30Y ~5.60%; 30Y auction 5.618%, bid-to-cover 2.54; Brent ~$104 (+4%).
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: a Financial Times report that OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue is near $50 billion, about $20 billion below the figure that had circulated, sent the Philadelphia chip index down 3.4% and the Nasdaq down 1.25%, its worst day since mid-August. Nvidia fell 2.9%, Micron 4.8%, Intel 5.3% and Oracle 5.5%. The S&P 500 fell 0.47% to 7,765.36 and the Dow rose 0.1%. The $22 billion thirty-year sold at 5.618% with a 2.54 bid-to-cover, and the ten-year eased about 5 basis points to near 5.23%. Brent rose about 4% to near $104 on Iranian tanker attacks and hurricane shut-ins, holding most of the gain after President Trump said there would be no strike on Iran before the midterms.

What it means: Wednesday's selling followed yields; Thursday's came with yields falling, which points to doubt about AI revenue rather than borrowing costs. The report does not by itself show AI hardware demand slowing: OpenAI's figure is net revenue and the higher number apparently used a gross measure. This morning's report was right on oil and wrong on yields, which fell rather than pressing Wednesday's highs.

What would change the picture: chip stocks recovering most of Thursday's losses before CPI on October 14 would mark the selling as a one-headline event. A second down day, or more OpenAI-linked financing at Broadcom or Oracle, would show the market reconsidering what OpenAI can pay for. An S&P 500 close under 7,666.45 would show the weakness spreading to the broad index. Note: news sites could not be opened from this run, so figures rest on search summaries of the cited sources; Russell 2000, VIX and DXY closes were unavailable.
verdict.lede_short: The Nasdaq fell 1.25%, its worst day since mid-August, after a report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is near $50 billion, about $20 billion below what had circulated, and chip stocks lost 3.4%. Treasury yields fell after a solid thirty-year sale, so the selling was about AI revenue, not interest rates. If chip stocks win back the losses before Wednesday's inflation report, it was one headline; an S&P 500 close under 7,666 would show it spreading.

supporting_data.label: The Nasdaq fell 1.25% to 27,193.34, its worst day since mid-August, after the FT reported OpenAI's annualized revenue near $50 billion against about $70 billion previously cited — the largest AI customer's revenue is in question, not borrowing costs.
Nvidia fell 2.9%, Micron 4.8% and Oracle 5.5% as the chip index lost 3.4% — the companies most exposed to OpenAI's spending fell hardest.
The $22 billion thirty-year sold at 5.618% with a 2.54 bid-to-cover and 72.3% to indirect bidders — a second long-dated sale this week found buyers at 2002-era yields.
The ten-year fell about 5 basis points to near 5.23% and the thirty-year to 5.602% — yields fell and tech fell anyway, so rates did not drive the day.

Oil jumped more than 5% before paring gains after President Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms — Brent still ended about 4% higher near $104 on tanker attacks and hurricane shut-ins.
Initial jobless claims fell to 197,000 against about 200,000 expected — no labour-market reason for the Fed to wait, with December hike odds near 69% on FedWatch.

watchlist_mentions.note: Fell 2.9% as the chip index lost 3.4% on the FT report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is near $50 billion; fell less than Micron (-4.8%) and Oracle (-5.5%).
Down about 1.8% over 24 hours to about $81,745 on Crypto.com, low $80,320; a third day lower, this time moving with tech while yields fell.

trade_setups.thesis: The chip index fell 3.4% on one report that OpenAI's revenue is about $20 billion below what had circulated, with the most OpenAI-exposed names (Micron, Oracle) falling most. Whether the market treats it as a measurement question or a demand question is unresolved.
trade_setups.invalidation: Recovery of most of the losses by Tuesday would mark a one-headline event; a second down day or more OpenAI-linked financing at Broadcom or Oracle would show the market repricing AI demand.

trade_setups.thesis: The index is 0.7% below its October 6 record of 7,818.93 at 7,765.36, with the Dow higher; the selling so far is concentrated in AI suppliers.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close under 7,666.45 would show weakness spreading to the broad index; holding it through CPI with tech recovering leaves Thursday as a sector sell-off.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent near $104 with the ten-year at about 5.23% is an unusual pairing after two auctions found buyers. September CPI tests whether the oil rise reaches core inflation and December hike odds near 69%.
trade_setups.invalidation: A hot core CPI would bring the ten-year back toward 5.331%; Brent under $100 on IEA release details or a quieter Gulf would take pressure off yields.
trade_setups.horizon: October 14-15, CPI and the IEA board
